title: Crispy Parmesan Zucchini Fries That Actually Stay Crunchy
description: Skip the soggy squash. These crispy parmesan zucchini fries bake up crunchy in the oven and pair with a quick garlic mayo. Zero deep frying required.
story: I honestly didn't think zucchini could ever hold its own as a fry. The first time I tried making these in my tiny apartment kitchen, I didn't salt the squash first and ended up with a sad, soggy pile of green mush that stuck to my baking sheet. But after tweaking the method, I finally nailed a batch with a genuinely crunchy parmesan crust that doesn't need a deep fryer. Working long hours means I refuse to scrub a greasy mess at 9 PM, so this entire recipe uses just one baking sheet lined with foil. Toss them in the oven, whip up a fast garlic mayo using what's already in the fridge, and you've got a snack that disappears in under five minutes.
ingredients: 3 medium-sized zucchini, cut into uniform matchstick fries
1/2 cup all-purpose flour (King Arthur is my go-to)
1 cup plain panko breadcrumbs for maximum crunch
3/4 cup freshly grated parmesan cheese (not the green shaker bottle)
instructions: Step 1: Preheat your oven to 425°F and line a rimmed baking sheet with heavy-duty aluminum foil. Place a wire cooling rack right on top of the sheet so air circulates underneath.
Step 2: Set up a breading station with three shallow bowls. Put the flour in the first, beaten eggs in the second, and mix the panko, grated parmesan, garlic powder, and kosher salt in the third.
Step 3: Dredge each zucchini stick lightly in flour, dip it into the egg, and then press it firmly into the panko-parm mixture so the coating sticks securely.
Step 4: Arrange the coated fries in a single layer on the wire rack without crowding them. Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until the crust turns deeply golden and smells nutty.
proHack: Don't skip patting your zucchini dry with paper towels before breading. Zucchini holds a ton of moisture, and any extra surface water will steam the breadcrumbs instead of letting them crisp up.
storage: Truthfully, these are best eaten right off the baking sheet. If you have leftovers, store them in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days, but reheat them in a 400°F toaster oven for 5 minutes to bring back the crunch.

faqs.question: Can I use Italian breadcrumbs instead of panko?
faqs.answer: You can, but the fries won't be nearly as crunchy. Panko has a lighter flake that toasts up better in the oven. If you only have regular breadcrumbs, mix in a handful of crushed cornflakes for extra texture.

faqs.question: How do I prevent my zucchini fries from getting soggy?
faqs.answer: Crowding the pan is the main culprit—it traps steam and ruins the crust. Give each fry some breathing room on the wire rack, and never cover them with foil after they come out of the oven.
